title: Compatibility and global solvability of the d-bar equation
notes: Given the coefficients \(\alpha_j\), the notes ask when \(u_{\bar z_j}=\alpha_j\) is soluble and how \(u\) depends on them; they write the cross-derivative compatibility conditions.
statement: Let \(\Omega\Subset\mathbb C^n\) have \(C^\infty\) strongly pseudoconvex boundary and let \(\alpha=\sum_j\alpha_j\,d\bar z_j\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega;\Lambda^{0,1})\). If \(\partial\alpha_j/\partial\bar z_k=\partial\alpha_k/\partial\bar z_j\), there is \(u\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega)\) with \(\bar\partial u=\alpha\); the canonical solution is \(u=\bar\partial^*N_1\alpha\). Without a global condition on \(\Omega\), compatibility alone need not give global solvability.
reconstruction: The global strong pseudoconvexity and smoothness assumptions are supplied from the ensuing argument. The notes begin with only a bounded domain; they do not state a general necessary-and-sufficient theorem for arbitrary domains.
fate: Already part of the expository framework in \citet{kohn1963potential}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, the precise statement is a standard established result or definition.

title: The complex tangent space and Levi form
notes: A defining function \(r\) is negative inside \(M\); the complex tangent vectors satisfy \(\sum r_{z_j}a^j=0\), and the displayed Hermitian form is \(\sum r_{z_i\bar z_j}a^i\bar a^j\).
statement: For a \(C^2\) real defining function with \(dr\ne0\) on \(\partial\Omega\), the complex tangent space at \(p\) is \(\ker\partial r(p)\). Its Levi form is \(\mathcal L_r(p;a)=\sum_{j,k}r_{z_j\bar z_k}(p)a_j\bar a_k\); strong pseudoconvexity means positivity for every nonzero complex tangent vector. Multiplying \(r\) by a positive smooth factor multiplies this restricted form by that factor.
reconstruction: The sign convention depends on \(\Omega=\{r<0\}\); positivity on the full ambient complex tangent space is not required.
fate: Already part of the expository framework in \citet{kohn1963potential}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, the precise statement is a standard established result or definition.

title: A local holomorphic support function
notes: Positivity of the Levi form is used to construct a holomorphic polynomial \(W\) whose zero set touches the boundary at \(p\) and otherwise lies outside the domain near \(p\).
statement: At a strongly pseudoconvex point \(p\) of a \(C^2\) boundary, a holomorphic polynomial \(W\) of degree at most two can be chosen with \(W(p)=0\), \(dW(p)\ne0\), and \(W(z)\ne0\) on \((\overline\Omega\cap U)\setminus\{p\}\), after shrinking \(U\). One obtains \(W\) from the holomorphic part of the second-order Taylor expansion of a suitably modified defining function.
reconstruction: A quadratic change in the defining function can make the real estimate strict in all relevant directions. The conclusion is local; the sketch does not prove global pseudoconvexity.
fate: Already part of the expository framework in \citet{kohn1963potential}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, the precise statement is a standard established result or definition.

title: Globalizing the local pole
notes: With a cut-off \(g=1\) near \(p\), the notes solve \(\bar\partial u=\bar\partial(g/W)\) and form \(h=u-g/W\). The final sentence attributes noncontinuation to \(u\).
statement: Under the preceding smooth strongly pseudoconvex domain assumptions, choose \(g\) supported in the support-function neighbourhood. The form \(\alpha=\bar\partial(g/W)\), extended by zero, is smooth on \(\overline\Omega\) and \(\bar\partial\)-closed. A smooth solution \(u\) gives a holomorphic \(h=u-g/W\) on \(\Omega\) with a singularity at \(p\), so \(h\) does not extend holomorphically across \(p\).
reconstruction: It is \(h\), not the globally smooth correction \(u\), whose boundary singularity is forced. Smoothness of \(\alpha\) follows because \(\bar\partial g=0\) near the only local zero of \(W\).
fate: Already part of the expository framework in \citet{kohn1963potential}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, the precise statement is a standard established result or definition.

title: The Dolbeault complex
notes: The spaces \(a^{p,q}\) of forms and the arrows \(a^{p,q-1}\to a^{p,q}\to a^{p,q+1}\) are written with differential \(\bar\partial\).
statement: On a complex manifold, \(C^\infty\) differential forms split by bidegree and \(\bar\partial:A^{p,q}\to A^{p,q+1}\) satisfies \(\bar\partial^2=0\). On a domain with boundary the maximal \(L^2\) realizations form a Hilbert complex; domains must be imposed before defining Hilbert adjoints.
reconstruction: The notes alternate \(a\) and \(\alpha\) as space letters. The Hilbert completion and operator domains are made explicit here.
fate: Already part of the expository framework in \citet{kohn1963potential}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, the precise statement is a standard established result or definition.

title: The Neumann quadratic form and canonical solution
notes: The quadratic form is \(Q(\varphi,\psi)=(\bar\partial\varphi,\bar\partial\psi)+(\bar\partial^*\varphi,\bar\partial^*\psi)\); a positive higher-order equation is proposed to solve the first-order compatible system.
statement: On \(L^2\) forms, put \(\mathcal D(Q)=\mathcal D(\bar\partial)\cap\mathcal D(\bar\partial^*)\). The closed nonnegative form defines the self-adjoint \(\bar\partial\)-Neumann Laplacian \(\Box=\bar\partial\bar\partial^*+\bar\partial^*\bar\partial\). If its inverse \(N_q\) exists on the orthogonal complement of its harmonic kernel, a closed \((p,q)\)-form orthogonal to that kernel is solved by \(\bar\partial^*N_q\alpha\).
reconstruction: The first-order equation follows using the complex identity and commutation with \(N\), not merely by solving an arbitrary positive second-order equation. The displayed domain in the notebook must also include \(\mathcal D(\bar\partial)\).
fate: Already part of the expository framework in \citet{kohn1963potential}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, the precise statement is a standard established result or definition.

title: The boundary estimate and its limitations
notes: The estimate \(\int_{\partial M}|\varphi|^2\,dS\le C Q(\varphi,\varphi)\) is displayed, followed by the warning that it does not control the sum of squares of all first derivatives.
statement: For a bounded smooth strongly pseudoconvex domain in \(\mathbb C^n\), \(q\ge1\), and smooth \((p,q)\)-forms satisfying the \(\bar\partial^*\) boundary condition, the boundary \(L^2\) norm is bounded by \(C Q\). More generally on a strongly pseudoconvex manifold an added \(L^2\) term or projection away from harmonic forms is needed. For \(0<q<n\), this is not a full \(H^1\) coercive estimate; at top antiholomorphic degree the boundary condition is of Dirichlet type.
reconstruction: \ours\ The degree and geometric hypotheses are indispensable: at \(q=0\), nonzero holomorphic functions can have \(Q=0\) and a nonzero boundary norm. The notebook's one-dimensional comparison refers to the top-degree situation.
fate: Already part of the expository framework in \citet{kohn1963potential}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, the precise statement is a standard established result or definition.

title: A reference to general overdetermined systems
notes: The notes refer to work of Spencer on general overdetermined systems but give no operator class or statement.
statement: No unique theorem about general overdetermined systems can be extracted. The identifiable idea is to exploit a differential complex and its compatibility operator when reducing a first-order system to a second-order variational problem.
reconstruction: This is a programme-level reference, not a statement that every overdetermined system is solved by the Neumann construction.
fate: \citet{kohn1963potential} discusses the related complex Neumann work and cites Kohn--Spencer, but this does not identify which general Spencer result the speaker meant.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, the cited survey and its references establish the context; the notebook reference remains underdetermined.

title: The Kohn-Rossi extension reference
notes: The notes name Kohn and Rossi, Annals of Mathematics 1965, and emphasize holomorphic continuation of forms into the domain.
statement: A precise special case is: if \(\Omega\Subset\mathbb C^n\), \(n\ge2\), has connected smooth strongly pseudoconvex boundary, every smooth CR function on \(\partial\Omega\) is the boundary value of a holomorphic function smooth on \(\overline\Omega\). Extension for higher-degree forms requires the appropriate tangential compatibility and cohomological conditions.
reconstruction: The function statement is a safe modern specialization, not a transcription of the unspecified assertion about all forms. No unrestricted forms-extension theorem is attributed to this one-line entry.
fate: The named article is \citet{kohnrossi1965extension}; its bibliographic identity is confirmed in Kohn's author bibliography. The original theorem text was not obtained in this search.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, the function-extension theorem is established; the exact higher-form assertion intended here remains unspecified.

title: Complete surfaces need not satisfy the closed Gauss-Bonnet equality
notes: A paraboloid is given as a complete, nonclosed surface with \(C=2\pi\) and \(\chi=1\); a second schematic surface is marked with a strict inequality.
statement: The graph \(z=x^2+y^2\), with its induced metric, is complete, is homeomorphic to \(\mathbb R^2\), and has total Gaussian curvature \(2\pi\). Completeness alone does not force equality: the Euclidean plane has \(\chi=1\) and total curvature zero.
reconstruction: \oursComputed\ The plane is a simple explicit replacement for the unnamed strict-inequality sketch, not an identification of that drawing. For the paraboloid, \(K=4/(1+4r^2)^2\), \(dA=r\sqrt{1+4r^2}\,dr\,d\theta\), whose integral is \(2\pi\).
fate: Already part of the expository framework in \citet{cohnvossen1935curvature}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, the precise statement is a standard established result or definition.

title: Cohn-Vossen's inequality
notes: The statement is abbreviated to \(C\le2\pi\chi\) for every complete surface.
statement: If a connected complete boundaryless Riemannian surface has finite topological type and integrable Gaussian curvature, then \(\int_M K\,dA\le2\pi\chi(M)\). The original formulation permits the corresponding well-defined total-curvature limit; absolute integrability is a convenient sufficient hypothesis here.
reconstruction: Finite topological type and existence of total curvature are supplied. Without a meaningful integral and Euler characteristic the unqualified expression is not a theorem.
fate: This is the pre-existing result in \citet[Theorem 6]{cohnvossen1935curvature}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, the precise statement is a standard established result or definition.

title: Finn's proposed equality with a defect term
notes: The sole statement about Finn's own aim is to replace the inequality by an equality.
statement: The entry does not specify the class of metrics, the ends, or a proposed defect invariant. Consequently no unique equality theorem can be reconstructed from it.
reconstruction: An identity obtained simply by defining a defect as \(2\pi\chi-\int K\,dA\) would be tautological; assigning Finn a particular geometric formula requires information absent here.
fate: The title and date of \citet{finn1965conformal} fit the discussion, but the accessible publisher record establishes metadata, not the equality intended in this notebook.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, the search identifies a likely contemporaneous publication context, not an unambiguously formulated unresolved problem.

title: Brouwer's theorem among the fixed-point applications
notes: Brouwer's theorem is listed among the results contained in the proposed fixed-point theory.
statement: Every continuous map from a closed finite-dimensional real ball to itself has a fixed point. Its relation to Lefschetz theory uses homotopy invariance and a suitable compact-space formulation; the smooth transverse elliptic-complex formula itself is not directly a theorem about arbitrary maps of a ball.
reconstruction: The ball, continuity, and finite-dimensionality are supplied. The entry gives only the name and does not record the reduction.
fate: Already part of the expository framework in \citet{atiyahbott1964notes}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, the precise statement is a standard established result or definition.

title: Lefschetz's fixed-point theorem in the applications list
notes: The ordinary Lefschetz formula is named before elliptic complexes are defined.
statement: For a self-map \(f\) of a finite polyhedron, a nonzero Lefschetz number \(\sum_q(-1)^q\operatorname{tr}(f^*:H^q(X;\mathbb Q)\to H^q(X;\mathbb Q))\) forces a fixed point. For a smooth map of a closed manifold with nondegenerate fixed points, this number is \(\sum_p\operatorname{sgn}\det(I-df_p)\).
reconstruction: These are precise familiar versions of the name in the notes; their derivation is discussed in record 65.
fate: Already part of the expository framework in \citet{atiyahbott1964notes}.
